name: PCTG
nozzleTemp: 250–265 °C (house baseline — confirm against the spool label)
drying: Dry at 65 °C for 8 h if stored open > 2 weeks or if stringing
enclosure: Open or closed — no enclosure required
useCases: Primary workhorse: structural brackets, gearbox plates, electronics shields. This is the default answer for an on-robot part.
notes: Clearer, tougher, and far faster than PETG with the same easy handling. Highest volumetric flow in the lineup — the material to pick when print throughput matters.

name: PETG-GF (Glass Fiber)
drying: Dry at 65 °C for 8 h — standard PETG precaution
useCases: High-rigidity motor mounts, dead-axle spacers, and stiff structural brackets — anywhere deflection matters more than toughness.
notes: Glass fill buys stiffness at the cost of some impact toughness — pick PCTG when the part takes hits, PETG-GF when it must not flex. Abrasive: hardened nozzle only, no 0.2 mm.

name: TPU, Shore 72D
maxSpeed: 40–80 mm/s — cap volumetric flow at ≤ 6 mm³/s on the Bambu fleet
useCases: Direct-impact armor, intake rollers, pulleys, hard stops, and bumper brackets — anything that takes a hit and must not shatter.
notes: 72D is a structural TPU, not a squishy one — it prints and bolts like a rigid plastic but absorbs impact instead of cracking. Direct-drive extruders only; feed from an external spool holder.

name: PPA-GF (Glass Fiber Nylon)
drying: Mandatory, every session. 80 °C for 4–6 h before use
enclosure: Required — heated chamber 60–80 °C. H2D / X2D only.
useCases: Extreme-load gearbox blocks and high-temp mounts (185 °C+ HDT). The escalation material when PCTG and PETG-GF have actually failed.
notes: Glass-filled nylon — immune to Loctite and the only material here that holds strength near the curing oven. Needs a respirator for post-processing and mentor sign-off to run.

name: PLA / PLA Basic
brands: Bambu PLA Basic, Bambu PLA Matte, ELEGOO PLA+, 3D-Fuel Pro PLA
drying: Usually not needed; 50 °C for 8 h if stringing
enclosure: Open — lid OFF or door open on Bambu (heat creep)
useCases: Prototypes, fit checks, jigs, drill guides, and cosmetic parts — plus the dual-nozzle support interface material. Not a functional robot part.
notes: Softens ~55 °C, brittle under impact, and creeps under bolt tension — prototype in PLA, ship in PCTG. Its other job is Nozzle 2: PLA will not weld to polyurethanes or copolyesters, which is what makes the zero-gap support trick work.

name: PETG / PETG HF
tierLabel: On the shelf — use it up
plate: Textured PEI (NEVER smooth PEI without glue — it welds)
drying: 65 °C for 8 h — hygroscopic; dry if stored open > 2 weeks
useCases: Perfectly good for brackets, covers, and guards — it is what we printed on-robot for years. Burn through open spools before starting new PCTG.
notes: Superseded by PCTG for new designs — PCTG is tougher and prints roughly twice as fast — but there is nothing wrong with a PETG part. Use the stock we have, then reorder PCTG.

name: TPU 95A / TPE (Flexible)
tierLabel: On the shelf — use it up
brands: HATCHBOX TPU 95A, PRILINE TPU, eSUN TPE-83A
drying: Required. 55–65 °C for 6–8 h — wet TPU bubbles and strings badly
useCases: Genuinely squishy parts: gaskets, belt guards, vibration dampers, soft grippers. Where you want compliance rather than impact strength.
notes: Different job than 72D — 95A is soft and stretchy, 72D is rigid armor. Keep 95A for sealing and damping; do not use it where a bolt clamps through. External spool holder only, retraction off or tiny.

name: PA-CF / PPA-CF (Carbon Fiber Nylon)
tierLabel: On the shelf — not for impact parts
brands: Bambu PAHT-CF, Bambu PPA-CF, Bambu PET-CF, Siraya Fibreheart PPA-CF
drying: Mandatory, every session. 80 °C for 12 h; store in a dry box
useCases: Static high-stiffness parts that never take a shock load: sensor mounts, electronics trays, fixturing. Use up the spools we own here.
notes: Very stiff and strong in tension, but chopped carbon fibers act as micro-stress risers under impact — CF parts shatter along layer lines in a collision. Pick PPA-GF or 72D TPU for anything that gets hit. Hardened nozzle and gears required; carbon dust means gloves.

name: PC (Polycarbonate)
tierLabel: On the shelf — keep away from Loctite
brands: Bambu PC, PRILINE PC, PRILINE PC-CF
plate: Smooth PEI or textured PEI + glue stick
useCases: Heat-resistant, optically clear, non-threadlocked parts: light pipes, guards near warm motors, curing-oven fixturing. Use up existing spools here.
notes: PC crazes and cracks on contact with anaerobic threadlockers (Loctite 242/262) — never use it on a joint that gets threadlocked. Warps aggressively; leave parts in the warm chamber until fully cool. High fumes: ventilate.
